dedupe_keys.name: multi vector simulator local energy system tool

description: The Multi-Vector Simulator is the Reiner Lemoine Institute's modelling tool for local sector-coupled energy systems in the E-LAND project. It combines electricity, heat and other energy carriers to evaluate technology mixes, costs and climate effects under user-supplied demand and resource data. Inputs are local assets, technology parameters and time series; outputs are dispatch, investment and performance measures for the chosen system. Spatial coverage is an island, district or comparable local network, with temporal resolution determined by the configured series. The GPL-2.0 source is free through GitHub and PyPI, with stable and development documentation. A caveat is that the README says the code remains under development, so users should pin a release and check model assumptions before using results for a larger project. It can compare decentralised generation, storage and flexibility choices in capacity-planning simulations. The catalogue's model-messageix-framework is a broader energy-scenario framework, not an underlying dependency. This review did not run or validate an E-LAND scenario.
